about: What a token costs, per backend and per model ([[REQ-292]]).
WHY IT IS A DOCUMENT AND NOT A TABLE OF CONSTANTS, and the reason is
`backends.json`'s exactly: a price is the second fastest-moving fact in the
system after a model ID, and the two change together. lagrange-framework
BUG-49 opened the seam for the first of them; this is the same seam used for
the second, so a repricing is an edit to this file and nothing else. It sits
beside `backends.json` because a `model` changed there without a rate added
here is the one edit that silently stops a turn being priced.
KEYED BY (BACKEND, MODEL), NEVER BY MODEL ALONE. Two levels, because a
provider is a thing this product must be able to acquire a second of. A table
keyed by model would have to be REWRITTEN the day a second backend arrives —
every entry re-homed under a provider that was previously implicit — rather
than extended by one object. The backend names are the framework's own
(`claude`, `chatgpt` in `defaults/backends.json`), so this file cannot key a
provider that does not exist, and `turn_spend.backend` records which one
actually ran.
FOUR RATES AND NOT ONE, because the request is billed from four counters. A
cached prefix is read at roughly a tenth of the full input rate and written at
rather more than it, so a single `input` rate cannot express the shape of a
long conversation at all — it would price the thing this whole ticket exists
to make visible as though caching were not happening.
UNITS: US DOLLARS PER MILLION TOKENS, which is how every provider publishes
them, so a rate can be copied off a pricing page without arithmetic in
between. That unit is also what makes the settled figure cheap and exact:
cost in MICROS (millionths of a dollar) is `tokens x rate`, summed over the
four counters, with no division and therefore no rounding until the end.
A PAIR THIS FILE DOES NOT NAME IS NOT AN ERROR. The row is still written, its
four raw counters intact, with `cost_micros` NULL — `measured but not priced`,
which is recoverable later from the counters. A zero would not be: it would
claim a turn was free, which is the one thing a meter must never say.
THE NUMBERS ARE PUBLISHED LIST RATES AT THE TIME OF WRITING and carry no
contracted discount. They are configuration: correcting one is an edit here,
and a past period's bill does not move when they change, because
`cost_micros` is settled at write time and stored.
